newsitem.title: USA: Dollar down at U.S. noon on BOJ rumors, NAPM drop.
newsitem.headline: Dollar down at U.S. noon on BOJ rumors, NAPM drop.

text.p: The dollar was weaker, but off session lows at midday, buffeted by rumors of Bank of Japan (BOJ) intervention to boost the yen, talk of options-linked selling and a decline in a key gauge of U.S. manufacturing activity, currency experts said.
The greenback's descent accelerated as stop-loss sell orders were triggered against the mark and yen, according to traders.
"There were rumors earlier that the Bank of Japan was intervening," said Richard Vullo, a vice president at Bayerische Hypobank.
Vullo said dollar/yen led the way down and took dollar/mark with it.
Some market players reported the rumor as simple rate-checking by the BOJ. But regardless of the talk, market players agreed the BOJ rumors were likely untrue.
The BOJ office in New York was not available to comment on the market rumors.
The dollar tumbled briefly to 126.12 yen and 1.7165 marks.
By noon, the U.S. currency had trimmed to losses to trade at 126.60/65 yen and 1.7205/10 marks, down from 126.99/04 yen and 1.7253/58 marks at the open.
The dollar's started to tumble in earnest shortly after 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. Around that time, the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) released its key index of manufacturing activity.
Some currency experts linked the dollar declines to that report, but others tied the greenback's drop to options-related selling.
"Apparently, someone was buying up dollars to knock in an option and didn't succeed and had to sell them off," said a dealer, adding that the option supposedly expired at 1000 EDT.

The NAPM manufacturing activity index slid to 54.2 in April from 55.0 in March, the new orders component fell to 57.9 from 60.3, the prices index slipped to 49.6 from 50.9 and the production component edged lower to 56.6 from 56.8.
Prior to the NAPM data, the U.S. Labor Department reported first-time state jobless claims rose 28,000 to 347,000 in the week ended April 26.
Hillel Waxman, a first vice president of Bank Leumi Trust Co of New York, noted that the rise in jobless claims could be attributed in part to floods and strikes.
Still, Waxman noted the increase in jobless claims set a negative tone for the dollar.
The NAPM numbers, he said, feed the mentality that the Federal Reserve is not going to hike interest rates near-term.

"That mentality with the...lack of anybody in the market place is what I think just pushed the dollar through the 1.72 (marks)," Waxman said. "I don't think (the dollar will) close below it. I think you bounce right back over it."
U.S. central bank policymakers are scheduled to meet next on May 20.
Many European market participants were absent from their desks because of the May Day holiday.
In other trade, the dollar fell to 1.4675/85 Swiss francs at midday from 1.4700/05 at the open.
Sterling inched up to $1.6235/45 from $1.6233/43.
The dollar fell to Canadian $1.3889/94 from C$1.3948/53.
